title: Critical: Private documents are served without authentication
block:
### API-01 — Critical: Private documents are served without authentication

**Severity:** Critical: · **Category:** security · **Location:** `backend/app/main.py:67–70,97–101`

```python
app.mount("/storage", StaticFiles(directory=settings.STORAGE_PATH), name="storage")
response.headers["Cache-Control"] = "public, max-age=86400"
```

The entire storage tree is exposed by a public ASGI mount. Document uploads use the same root and return predictable `/storage/student/{owner_id}/{filename}` or `/storage/mentor/{owner_id}/{filename}` paths; a caller can fetch a known or guessed private document URL without the `/documents/` listing guard. The student-only-own expectation is explicit in `test_documents.py:56–63`, yet that test only checks metadata listing. StaticFiles performs filesystem safety checks, not this application's authentication or ownership checks; public caching additionally allows copies to survive later revocation.

**Fix:** Mount only intentionally public avatar/course-image directories. Serve documents through `GET /documents/{id}/download` that loads the document, rejects deletion, applies the canonical role/object policy and returns a private/no-store response. For object storage, issue short-lived private signed URLs after the same check. Add anonymous, different-student and revoked-document download tests using the returned file path; checking list visibility alone is insufficient.
verification: Confirmed public mount and public caching; download guard absent. Existing listing policy must be reused explicitly.

title: Critical: Restricted onboarding tokens receive ordinary account privileges
block:
### API-02 — Critical: Restricted onboarding tokens receive ordinary account privileges

**Severity:** Critical: · **Category:** security · **Location:** `backend/app/core/deps.py:33–52,55–77`; `backend/app/api/v1/auth.py:75–82`

```python
payload = jwt.decode(token, settings.JWT_SECRET_KEY, algorithms=["HS256"])
user_id = int(payload.get("sub"))
...
return user
```

`get_current_user` ignores the signed `scope` claim. `AuthService.login`, `refresh` and `verify_code` emit `scope="must_set_password"`, but all normal route guards consume this dependency and accept those tokens. The separate `check_must_set_password` has no callers. A verified onboarding token for a superadmin can therefore create/delete users or call finance routes before completing password setup. Checking only the current DB flag would also be insufficient: a previously issued restricted token must remain restricted after `must_set_password` becomes false.

**Fix:** Introduce a typed authenticated principal carrying validated token purpose/scope. Make the default application dependency reject restricted scope and users awaiting setup. Use a separate explicit dependency for `/auth/set-password` that accepts the permitted setup token; preserve the separate password-reset-token verifier and its token-type checks. Regression tests must cover ordinary routes for each restricted role, successful setup, and reuse of the original restricted token after setup.
verification: Confirmed ordinary dependency ignores scope, setup guard unused; retain restriction even after setup.

title: Critical: Scheduler endpoints disable authentication when configuration is missing
block:
### API-03 — Critical: Scheduler endpoints disable authentication when configuration is missing

**Severity:** Critical: · **Category:** security · **Location:** `backend/app/api/v1/cron.py:9–14,17–32`

```python
if settings.CRON_SECRET and x_cloud_scheduler_secret != settings.CRON_SECRET:
    raise HTTPException(status_code=401, ...)
```

An unset or empty secret makes this condition false for every request. Configuration declares `CRON_SECRET` optional with default `None`, and these endpoints have no other application authentication. Under that valid configuration, anonymous requests can archive courses and trigger reminder work. This is a conditional vulnerability; the audit does not claim the deployed secret is absent.

**Fix:** Fail closed when the secret is absent, reject absent/mismatched headers and compare configured secrets with `hmac.compare_digest`. Require the configuration in production startup, or verify Cloud Scheduler OIDC with its expected audience. Use one `Depends(verify_cron_secret)` guard on the router. Test unset, empty, wrong, missing and correct credentials for both endpoints.
verification: Confirmed missing-secret fail-open branch; actual deployed secret unknown.

title: Verification-code resend has no throttling
block:
### API-04 — Verification-code resend has no throttling

**Severity:** Required (no prefix) · **Category:** security/performance · **Location:** `backend/app/api/v1/auth.py:66–72`

```python
async def resend_code(payload: ResendCodeRequest, db=Depends(get_db_session)):
    auth_service = AuthService(db)
    await auth_service.resend_code(payload.email)
```

Unlike login, verification and password-reset requests, this anonymous email-sending route applies no rate limit. The service overwrites the stored code and resets its attempt counter each time. Repeated requests can flood a pending user's inbox and invalidate a code immediately before the user submits it, as well as consume SMTP capacity. Service reads confirmed there is no hidden resend limiter.

**Fix:** Apply an email-based resend cooldown and a sender/global request budget before code generation; do not clear the resend limit on successful sending. Preserve the last valid code during the cooldown. Add tests proving repeated calls receive 429 and do not enqueue/send more email or overwrite the accepted code.
verification: Confirmed cited source mechanism and surrounding call path; static review, not a newly executed integration/load test.

title: Instance shutdown removes the shared Telegram webhook
block:
### API-05 — Instance shutdown removes the shared Telegram webhook

**Severity:** Required (no prefix) · **Category:** scalability/correctness · **Location:** `backend/app/main.py:23–41`

```python
await bot.set_webhook(...)
...
yield
...
await bot.delete_webhook()
```

The webhook belongs to the bot globally, while lifespan executes per process/Cloud Run instance. During scale-down or a rolling deployment, an old instance can delete the webhook after another live instance has registered it; Telegram delivery then stops despite a healthy serving instance. Startup/shutdown exceptions are also silently suppressed, so this loss has no visible application signal.

**Fix:** Register the webhook through a deployment/admin operation with one owner and remove unconditional deletion from instance shutdown. Close the local bot HTTP session during shutdown instead. Log registration failures with useful context, and test two overlapping application lifetimes: closing one must not delete the shared webhook.
verification: Confirmed cited source mechanism and surrounding call path; static review, not a newly executed integration/load test.

title: Telegram handler acknowledges failed updates as successful
block:
### API-06 — Telegram handler acknowledges failed updates as successful

**Severity:** Required (no prefix) · **Category:** quality/correctness · **Location:** `backend/app/api/v1/telegram.py:20–26`

```python
await dp.feed_update(bot, update)
except Exception as e:
    logger.error(...)
return {"status": "ok"}
```

Both invalid request JSON/schema and operational failures in handlers are caught by the same blanket handler and returned as HTTP 200. A temporary DB or Telegram/API failure therefore acknowledges an update that was not successfully handled, preventing Telegram's retry behavior. The existing webhook test only exercises the successful contact-binding path.

**Fix:** Handle malformed input with an explicit 400/422; allow transient processing failures to produce a retryable 5xx, or persist the update durably before acknowledging and process it with an idempotent background consumer. Test malformed updates, failed processing and successful retries without duplicate effects.
verification: Confirmed cited source mechanism and surrounding call path; static review, not a newly executed integration/load test.

title: Progress chart uses inconsistent populations and average rules
block:
### API-07 — Progress chart uses inconsistent populations and average rules

**Severity:** Required (no prefix) · **Category:** quality/correctness · **Location:** `backend/app/api/v1/courses.py:197–216,225–269,282–298`

```python
Enrollment.status == EnrollmentStatus.ACTIVE
j_summaries = [s for s in summaries if s.journal_id == j.id and s.max_period_score > 0]
avg_pct = round(sum(percentages) / len(journals), 2) if journals else 0.0
```

The student branch excludes only missing or zero-maximum summaries from their average, while the staff branch divides by every journal. A student with one 80% period and one missing/zero-maximum summary (for example, a journal that predates their enrollment) appears with 80% to themselves and 40% to staff. A positive `max_period_score` is not proof that grading occurred: preinitialized ungraded summaries can have a positive maximum and are counted by both branches. Class averages include all summaries, including withdrawn students, while `class_size` and rank include only active enrollments. Access deliberately allows any nondeleted enrollment, so a withdrawn student can receive a fallback rank of `class_size + 1`, an impossible position within the returned class size (including rank 1/class size 0).

**Fix:** Define the chart's roster and grading denominator once in a chart service, then use that policy for class averages, staff averages, rank and class size. If archived/withdrawn students may view their history, define their historical cohort or return an explicitly absent rank. Add a multi-student fixture with missing/zero-maximum summaries, preinitialized positive-maximum ungraded summaries and a withdrawn student, asserting the exact staff/student averages and valid rank semantics.
verification: Confirmed cited source mechanism and surrounding call path; static review, not a newly executed integration/load test.

title: Monetary inputs exceed the precision and range of persisted amounts
block:
### API-08 — Monetary inputs exceed the precision and range of persisted amounts

**Severity:** Required (no prefix) · **Category:** quality/correctness · **Location:** `backend/app/schemas/payment.py:16–21`; `backend/app/schemas/ledger.py:40–42,49–55,61–66,72–78`; `backend/app/schemas/course.py:32–42`

```python
amount: Decimal = Field(gt=0)
price: Decimal = Field(gt=0)
```

Decimal preserves exact input values but these schemas impose neither scale nor maximum digits. Persistence uses `Numeric(10, 2)` for ledger amounts and course prices. Isolated execution confirmed `PaymentCreate` accepts `0.001` and `100000000.00`; the service checks positivity before inserting the original amount. The first can become zero when stored and violate the positive-amount constraint; the second exceeds the column range. Validated requests can thus fail as DB errors, and extra fractional digits can silently change financial amounts.

**Fix:** Use one shared money input type with `Field(gt=0, max_digits=10, decimal_places=2)` for payment/refund/discount/adjustment/allocation and course-price inputs. If rounding is a product rule, perform it explicitly before positivity checks and document it. Add boundary tests for sub-cent amounts, three fractional digits, the maximum valid amount and an overflow amount; expect validation errors rather than database failures.
verification: Confirmed cited source mechanism and surrounding call path; static review, not a newly executed integration/load test.

title: Several regression tests do not exercise the invariant they claim
block:
### API-09 — Several regression tests do not exercise the invariant they claim

**Severity:** Required (no prefix) · **Category:** quality/tests · **Location:** `backend/app/tests/integration/test_student_cabinet_backend.py:119–156,159–206`; `backend/app/tests/integration/test_coverage_gaps.py:30–37,41–52`; `backend/app/tests/integration/test_documents.py:56–70`

```python
"""Test active vs archive bucket logic ... and rank calculation with ungraded period exclusion."""
...
assert course_entry["bucket"] == "active"
```

The bucket/rank test creates only an active course and asserts only that bucket; it never creates an archived/withdrawn enrollment, grades competing students or checks exclusion of ungraded periods. The roster-narrowing test seeds only one student, so returning every classmate still passes. The logout test never tries the token after logout, and the reset-confirm test sends `token` instead of the required `reset_token`, so its permitted 422 bypasses token verification entirely. Document visibility seeds just one document, so its length-one assertion cannot prove exclusion of another student's document. These are concrete missing behaviors, not a measured mutation score.

**Fix:** Seed adversarial second objects and assert absence of their identifiers; add graded/ungraded peers and archived/withdrawn enrollments with expected numeric results; test refresh replay and the rotated token after logout. Send a schema-valid invalid reset token and also exercise successful reset and replay according to the intended policy. Replace broad status alternatives with the specific expected code where fixture conditions are controlled.
verification: Confirmed cited source mechanism and surrounding call path; static review, not a newly executed integration/load test.

title: Optional: Move domain calculation and queries out of routers and complete typed response boundaries
block:
### API-10 — Optional: Move domain calculation and queries out of routers and complete typed response boundaries

**Severity:** Optional: · **Category:** maintainability/extensibility · **Location:** `backend/app/api/v1/courses.py:186–315`; `backend/app/api/v1/mentors.py:137–172`; `backend/app/api/v1/students.py:75–113`; `backend/app/api/v1/journals.py:22–29`; `backend/app/api/v1/finance.py:51,140–148`; `backend/app/core/deps.py:80–126`

```python
@router.get("/{id}/progress-chart")
...
select(func.avg(JournalStudentSummary.sum_score))
...
decorated = await finance_service._decorate_entries([entry])
```

The chart handler owns roster queries, ranking, colors and aggregation; mentor analytics owns three SQL calculations. Student/mentor profile handlers and course-access helpers reach directly into repositories/ORM state. This contradicts the documented controller/service/repository separation and creates multiple places to update grading and cohort policies. Generic `dict` responses for journal detail/chart/analytics and `List[dict]` for ledger history also discard the Pydantic/OpenAPI boundary used elsewhere. The finance router calls a private service method. Existing unused ownership helpers duplicate route-specific checks; `core.deps.get_storage_service` always returns local storage while the storage module has a separate configuration-aware factory, and neither dependency factory is wired into these service constructors.

**Fix:** Extract a `CourseProgressService` with an explicit repository result and a shared roster/grading policy; move mentor calculations into a repository-backed analytics service. Inject services through named `Depends` factories and expose a public decorated-payment operation. Add typed staff/student chart DTOs, journal-detail and ledger-history DTOs. Consolidate ownership policies and the storage factory once the intended policies are settled. Avoid extracting pass-through wrappers that merely relocate existing complexity.
verification: Confirmed router SQL/dict boundaries. Private finance call is at line 55, not cited line 51; corrected citation added.

block:
### API-11 — Optional: Bound aggregate responses and make chart work proportional to the data returned

**Severity:** Optional: · **Category:** scalability/performance · **Location:** `backend/app/api/v1/courses.py:194–216,239–259,282–308`; `backend/app/api/v1/finance.py:140–148,187–194`; `backend/app/api/v1/students.py:56–70`; `backend/app/api/v1/cron.py:17–32`

```python
summaries = list(summary_res.scalars().all())
for j in journals:
    j_summaries = [s for s in summaries if s.journal_id == j.id ...]
```

Chart retrieval materializes every enrollment and summary, and the student branch rescans the full summary list for each journal: O(J × S), with S commonly proportional to students × journals. Staff responses grow with students × journals. Ledger history, credits and student journal history expose uncapped lists. Scheduler handlers synchronously await whole maintenance jobs, keeping requests open and allowing overlapping scheduler retries. No load benchmark was run, so no latency claim is made; these are observable growth mechanisms.

**Fix:** Add date/period ranges and pagination to histories/credits; pre-index summaries by journal and student or compute class aggregates in SQL, returning only the student's series for their chart. Establish a product limit or paginated staff chart series. Enqueue maintenance jobs through the existing ARQ abstraction with stable deduplication keys and return an accepted job identifier; measure bounded fixtures and concurrent triggers before choosing cache TTLs.
verification: Confirmed cited source mechanism and surrounding call path; static review, not a newly executed integration/load test.

title: Optional: Align settings and phone validation with the project's declared input rules
block:
### API-12 — Optional: Align settings and phone validation with the project's declared input rules

**Severity:** Optional: · **Category:** quality/maintainability · **Location:** `backend/app/schemas/org_settings.py:15–18`; `backend/app/schemas/user.py:14–16,26–28,37–39`

```python
class OrgSettingsUpdate(BaseModel):
    org_name: Optional[str] = Field(None, min_length=1, max_length=255)
phone: Optional[str] = Field(None, pattern=r"^\+?[1-9]\d{1,14}$")
```

The settings input omits `extra="forbid"`; a payload such as `{"notify_paymnts": false}` is silently accepted as an empty update, despite the project requiring unknown inputs to fail. Every phone regex makes the leading plus optional, contrary to the documented strict E.164 representation; equivalent numbers can be stored differently. Isolated class checks reproduced both behaviors. This is a standards/consistency recommendation; the audit does not infer an additional security vulnerability from the format alone.

**Fix:** Add settings' missing extra-field configuration and share a normalized E.164 phone type that requires `+` (or a documented boundary normalizer that produces it). Add typo and phone-format tests and review existing stored values before enforcing canonical formatting.
verification: Confirmed cited source mechanism and surrounding call path; static review, not a newly executed integration/load test.

title: Critical: Refresh tokens are identical across users minted in the same second
block:
### BUS-01 — Critical: Refresh tokens are identical across users minted in the same second

**Severity:** Critical: · **Category:** security / quality · **Location:** `backend/app/core/security.py:60-72`; `backend/app/services/auth_service.py:41-51,69-83`.

```python
to_encode = {"exp": int(expire.timestamp()), "iat": int(now.timestamp())}
return jwt.encode(to_encode, settings.JWT_REFRESH_SECRET_KEY, algorithm="HS256")
```

There is no random identifier or subject. With the default lifetime, two calls in the same second produce identical signed tokens and hashes. Refresh resolves a user from the first matching nonrevoked database row, so an ordinary user's token can resolve another user's session, including an administrator. Same-second rotation also produces the old token again. The model's hash index is not unique; it does not prevent this. The orchestrator's isolated frozen-time execution reproduced the collision without importing the app.

**Fix:** generate a cryptographically random opaque token (`secrets.token_urlsafe(32)`) or add a random `jti` plus subject/type claims, bind lookup to the identity, and enforce token-hash uniqueness. Atomically claim/revoke the stored old token during rotation so two concurrent refreshes cannot both succeed. Add frozen-time tests for different users, rotation, replay and logout.
verification: Confirmed cited source mechanism and surrounding call path; static review, not a newly executed integration/load test.

title: Critical: Concurrent ledger writers can spend the same credit and refund beyond the payment
block:
### BUS-02 — Critical: Concurrent ledger writers can spend the same credit and refund beyond the payment

**Severity:** Critical: · **Category:** quality / scalability · **Location:** `backend/app/services/finance_service.py:165-177,271-324,736-770,785-857`.

```python
available = await self._entry_available(entry)
amount = min(available, needed)
self.db.add(Allocation(ledger_entry_id=entry.id, charge_id=charge.id, amount=amount))
```

Allocation totals, wallet amounts and cumulative refunds are checked with unlocked reads before inserts. Two transactions can both see a charge with 100 remaining and allocate 100; two refunds can both see 100 refundable and each refund 100. Allocation/ledger constraints only require positive individual amounts, and there is no lock, version check or aggregate constraint. Updating charge status afterward does not undo excess allocations. Sequential reconciliation tests never create simultaneous writers.

**Fix:** serialize every student financial mutation on a stable existing student/account row with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`, retain the lock through request commit, and use the same lock for schedule generation, withdrawal, allocation, refund and void. Add a unique partial constraint for one void per original payment and parallel PostgreSQL tests using separate sessions.
verification: Confirmed aggregate reads followed by inserts without stable shared writer lock; actual concurrent DB test pending.

title: Critical: A voided payment can still be refunded
block:
### BUS-03 — Critical: A voided payment can still be refunded

**Severity:** Critical: · **Category:** quality · **Location:** `backend/app/services/finance_service.py:717-770,866-878`.

```python
target = await self._get_payment_entry(payment_id)
already_refunded = Decimal(refunded_res.scalar() or 0)
max_refundable = target.amount - already_refunded
```

The target helper checks only that the row is a payment. Refund excludes prior refunds but never checks prior voids, whereas void explicitly rejects prior refunds. After voiding a payment, a cash refund is still accepted up to its full original amount. The void already removed its credit; the extra cash-out can reduce unrelated wallet credit and cash analytics. Existing lifecycle tests cover refund-then-void, not void-then-refund.

**Fix:** under BUS-02's lock, reject refund when a VOID exists for the target; centralize the reversible-payment eligibility rule. Test both reversal orders and assert no extra ledger/audit rows on rejection.
verification: Confirmed refund checks prior REFUND only; payment lookup does not exclude VOID.

### BUS-04 — Uploaded documents with the same filename overwrite previous documents

**Severity:** Required (no prefix) · **Category:** quality · **Location:** `backend/app/services/storage_service.py:40-62,112-120`; `backend/app/services/document_service.py:75-86,112-121`.

```python
filepath = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(target_dir, filename))
await path.write_bytes(file_content)
```

Storage keys use only entity type, owner ID and sanitized client filename, while each upload creates a distinct Document row. Uploading `test.pdf` twice for the same student, including in different journals, gives both rows the same path and replaces the first document's bytes. Deleting either document removes the other's file. GCS has the same key construction.

**Fix:** use an immutable UUID/object ID in each storage key while retaining the original filename as metadata. Stage replacement image objects under new keys and clean up old objects after DB commit. Test duplicate filenames and deletion independence.

title: Password reset grants can be reused after successful reset
block:
### BUS-05 — Password reset grants can be reused after successful reset

**Severity:** Required (no prefix) · **Category:** security · **Location:** `backend/app/services/auth_service.py:262-270,280-305`.

```python
to_encode = {"sub": email, "type": "password_reset", "exp": ..., "iat": ...}
user.password_hash = hash_password(new_password)
```

Confirmation only verifies signature/type/expiry and does not consume or revoke the grant. The same reset token can change the password repeatedly for five minutes, including after the user has completed recovery. Refresh-token revocation does not revoke this JWT.

**Fix:** issue a random single-use reset grant stored by hash, atomically claim it once, and apply password change/revocation in the transaction; alternatively bind a stored nonce/password version to the signed grant. Test reuse and simultaneous confirmation.
verification: Confirmed cited source mechanism and surrounding call path; static review, not a newly executed integration/load test.

title: Reset-code attempts and consumption are not atomic
block:
### BUS-06 — Reset-code attempts and consumption are not atomic

**Severity:** Required (no prefix) · **Category:** security / scalability · **Location:** `backend/app/services/auth_service.py:125-150,236-261`.

```python
raw_data = await redis_client.get(key)
data["attempts"] += 1
await redis_client.set(key, json.dumps(data), keepttl=True)
...
await redis_client.delete(key)
```

Parallel attempts read the same counter and overwrite the same increment, bypassing the five-attempt budget. Parallel correct submissions can both issue grants before either deletion is observed. Password-reset verification has no independent router rate limiter, so this directly weakens its only attempt limit; the separate limiter on initial verification does not make token consumption atomic.

**Fix:** move compare/increment/consume into one Redis Lua script, preserving expiry and returning a typed outcome. Test five concurrent failures and exactly one successful consume.
verification: Confirmed cited source mechanism and surrounding call path; static review, not a newly executed integration/load test.

### BUS-07 — Reminder calculations still use the retired payment model

**Severity:** Required (no prefix) · **Category:** quality / maintainability · **Location:** `backend/app/workers/tasks.py:209-225`.

func.sum(Payment.amount * (Decimal("1.0") - cast(Payment.discount_percent, Numeric) / Decimal("100.0")))

block:
### BUS-08 — Reminder logs mark queue acceptance as successful delivery

**Severity:** Required (no prefix) · **Category:** quality / scalability · **Location:** `backend/app/workers/tasks.py:42-46,235-251`; `backend/app/services/notification_service.py:120-129`.

```python
await enqueue_job("send_telegram_message", chat_id=..., text=text)
# caller subsequently records SENT
```

Reminder `send_func` only enqueues another task, so NotificationService records SENT before Telegram runs. The second task swallows TelegramForbiddenError/TelegramBadRequest and has no notification-log ID to mark a failure. Its transient failures also cannot update the first job's log. The user's notification history and retry budget therefore describe queue acceptance, not delivery.

**Fix:** have one delivery job own claim, send and final status, carrying a notification ID. Persist queued/in-flight states separately from sent, and record permanent failures in that same log. Test successful enqueue followed by failed delivery.

block:
### BUS-09 — Failed/revised notification rows can be sent by multiple workers

**Severity:** Required (no prefix) · **Category:** quality / scalability · **Location:** `backend/app/services/notification_service.py:77-102,120-135`.

```python
log = result.scalars().first()
log.attempts += 1
await self.db.commit()
await send_func(is_update)
```

The unique insert handles competing first inserts, but an existing FAILED row or revised SENT row has no exclusive claim. Two workers can read it, both increment attempts and both deliver. Committing before the send releases any potential transactional ownership; a crash after remote delivery and before the final commit also causes a resend.

**Fix:** use an atomic conditional update to claim a pending revision with a lease/claim token and finalize only that token. Document at-least-once semantics where Telegram offers no idempotency key, and distinguish revisions using a durable version. Test concurrent retries and abandoned claims.
verification: Confirmed cited source mechanism and surrounding call path; static review, not a newly executed integration/load test.

title: Exam notifications collide for siblings and suppress document-only updates
block:
### BUS-10 — Exam notifications collide for siblings and suppress document-only updates

**Severity:** Required (no prefix) · **Category:** quality · **Location:** `backend/app/workers/tasks.py:87-101,127-134,138-139`.

```python
related_entity_id=journal_id
if existing_log and existing_log.error_message != f"score:{summary.sum_score}":
```

The idempotency identity is recipient, type, journal and date. Two students in the same journal sharing a parent chat therefore share one notification row. If their sums match, the second is suppressed; if they differ, it is treated as a revision and retains the first student's user ID. A document upload delegates to the same worker, but a new document with an unchanged sum is suppressed too, so the attachment never reaches the parent.

**Fix:** key exam notifications by the student's summary ID (or explicit student+journal identity) and use a revision signature containing summary version and document identity. Test siblings with equal scores and a document added after an initial score notification.
verification: Confirmed cited source mechanism and surrounding call path; static review, not a newly executed integration/load test.

title: Jobs and analytics invalidation run before the business transaction commits
block:
### BUS-11 — Jobs and analytics invalidation run before the business transaction commits

**Severity:** Required (no prefix) · **Category:** quality / scalability · **Location:** `backend/app/services/journal_service.py:631-639`; `backend/app/services/document_service.py:94-107`; `backend/app/services/finance_service.py:543,606,645,714,783,857`; `backend/app/services/enrollment_service.py:133-169`.

```python
await sum_service.recalculate(journal_id, student_id)
await enqueue_job("send_exam_result_notification_task", student_id, journal_id)
```

The request session commits after the service returns. A fast worker can read the old score or fail to find a newly uploaded document; a later DB failure leaves a job for rolled-back work. Enqueue exceptions are silently discarded. Similarly, analytics keys are deleted before commit: a reader can repopulate them from old DB state and keep it for ten minutes after the write. Schedule generation and withdrawal change analytics inputs without invalidating at all.

### BUS-13 — Optimistic conflicts escape the journal's 409 handling

**Severity:** Required (no prefix) · **Category:** quality / scalability · **Location:** `backend/app/services/journal_service.py:479-512,622-632,708-724`; `backend/app/services/audit_service.py:37-43`; `backend/app/services/sum_calculation_service.py:118`.

...

    await self.db.flush()
except StaleObjectError: ...
...

SQLAlchemy version columns correctly detect conflicting writes, but the catch only surrounds one flush. title: Token lookup does not consume refresh tokens atomically
block:
### DATA-04 — Token lookup does not consume refresh tokens atomically

**Severity:** Required (no severity prefix in title) · **Categories:** security, quality.  
**Location:** `backend/app/repositories/sqlalchemy/refresh_token_repository.py:28–36`; defensive schema context `backend/app/models/refresh_token.py:13`.

The valid-token SELECT has no lock and returns the first matching row. Two transactions can read the same unrevoked token, both pass validity, then both rotate it: the subsequent ORM update filters by primary key, not by `revoked_at IS NULL`, and there is no version check. The auth service's read-then-revoke use confirms this concrete interleaving. The hash index is also nonunique, so persistence does not reject duplicate identities; the underlying token-generator collision is owned by the business/domain review and should be fixed there.

```python
query = select(RefreshToken).filter(
    RefreshToken.token_hash == token_hash,
    RefreshToken.revoked_at == None,
    RefreshToken.expires_at > now,
)
return result.scalars().first()
```

**Fix:** Add a repository `consume_valid_token` operation using `UPDATE ... WHERE token_hash = ... AND revoked_at IS NULL AND expires_at > ... RETURNING`, consumed once within the rotation transaction; no row means unauthorized. After fixing issuance and invalidating duplicate legacy tokens, add a unique token-hash constraint. Add a two-session simultaneous rotation test asserting exactly one success.

### PERF-BUS-01 — SMTP without a socket deadline retains request transactions and executor threads

**Impact: High. Category: async/concurrency. Review disposition: Required (no prefix).**
**Owned locations:** backend/app/services/email_service.py:24-34; backend/app/services/auth_service.py:111-121,169-177,219-232; backend/app/services/user_service.py:41-44,64-67.

**New path:** SMTP uses asyncio.to_thread, so it does not itself block the event loop. However smtplib.SMTP has no timeout argument here; inspection confirmed it defaults to Python's global socket timeout, which was None. Password-reset and resend perform user lookup before awaiting delivery; user creation flushes its INSERT before delivery. Request session context commits only after return. A stalled SMTP connect/read therefore retains the checked-out connection/transaction (and created-row locks where applicable) throughout the stall, as well as an executor thread. At A simultaneous stalled requests, up to A database connections and A executor tasks remain occupied, limited by the configured pools/executor; other requests then wait. Worker email delivery uses the same indefinite socket path. Cancellation of to_thread does not forcibly stop the underlying thread.

**Evidence:** the actual constructor, caller await order and yield-session commit boundary establish retention; no stalled service was contacted. This is distinct from the prior bcrypt/image blocking finding and from resend abuse.

**Corrected proposal:** Add a finite per-socket SMTP timeout and use a transactional mail outbox so user/reset business transactions finish without waiting for remote delivery. A bounded worker consumes the committed event; apply a total delivery deadline, finite attempts and queue-age/expiry policy so delayed verification codes are not sent after expiry. Keep the existing thread offload and CA-verifying TLS.

```python
with smtplib.SMTP(settings.SMTP_HOST, settings.SMTP_PORT, timeout=10) as server:
    server.starttls(context=ssl.create_default_context())
```

Timeout=10 is an illustrative budget to tune, not a measured optimum. Merely wrapping to_thread in asyncio.wait_for leaves the thread running; socket deadlines and bounded executor work are required. Do not commit arbitrary service sessions early to free the connection, since that would split the business transaction.

**Measure:** fault-inject SMTP connect/read stalls in an isolated harness; record transaction duration, pool checkout wait, active executor work and unrelated request p95/p99 at 1/10/30 concurrent mail requests. Confirm every stall terminates within the configured delivery budget and rolled-back user creation emits no deliverable outbox event. Repeat equal conditions after fixing; no timings were measured here.
verification: Confirmed SMTP offload, missing socket timeout and DB-before-mail await order. Pool impact remains unmeasured.

### PERF-DATA-03 — Scoring migration rewrites every summary at least twice in one migration transaction

**Impact:** Medium, size-dependent rollout risk. **Category:** database/concurrency/startup. **Review disposition:** Required (no prefix). **Location:** `backend/alembic/versions/d8e9f0a1b2c3_journal_scoring_redesign.py:15–65`; deployment coupling `.github/workflows/deploy-backend.yml:124–134`; `backend/scripts/gcp_deploy.sh:42–45`.

Additional bonus/exam clamps update B and X rows, so row-update operations are 2S+B+X, bounded by 4S. At S=1M, source therefore prescribes between 2M and 4M summary row updates, plus the journal update and constraint validation. This is a statement/row-operation model, not a timing or WAL-byte measurement. Alembic executes the revision transactionally; added-column locks and updates can block writers until commit. Both deploy paths proceed even when migrations fail, so timeout/lock failure may leave the old schema serving the new image.

**Evidence:** Four explicit summary UPDATE statements; two have no selective predicate beyond the valid FK join. The scripts' `alembic upgrade head || echo ...` suppresses failure. This is distinct from prior DATA-13's absent migration tests: newly included source proves rollout work/failure handling.

**Corrected-code proposal:** Preserve the original pre-clamp homework derivation while combining all summary transformations into one UPDATE when a measured maintenance window suffices. For large production datasets, use expand/backfill/validate phases with bounded batches and a forward-compatible application rollout; SQL expressions below show the one-pass logic, not a migration already tested.

```sql
UPDATE journal_student_summaries s
SET homework_score = s.sum_score - s.exam_score - s.bonus_score,
    attendance_score = s.attendance_count,
    bonus_score = LEAST(s.bonus_score, 20),
    exam_score = LEAST(s.exam_score, j.exam_max_score),
    max_period_score = s.total_lessons * 6 + j.exam_max_score,
    sum_score = (s.sum_score - s.exam_score - s.bonus_score)
                + s.attendance_count + LEAST(s.exam_score, j.exam_max_score)
                + LEAST(s.bonus_score, 20)
FROM journals j WHERE j.id = s.journal_id;
```

All RHS expressions refer to old row values; that preserves existing homework semantics. Make migration failure stop deployment; include tested settings/dependencies in the migration runner. Proposed measurement: representative sanitized database copy at 10k/100k/1M summaries; record affected rows, wall time, WAL delta, dead tuples, lock waits and ordinary writer p95 through the upgrade. Assert exact score outputs and constraint behavior before accepting a faster plan. No migration was run here.

### PERF-DATA-04 — Every paginated search pays COUNT and OFFSET work, including empty results

**Impact:** Medium. **Category:** database. **Review disposition:** Required (no prefix). **Location:** `backend/app/repositories/sqlalchemy/base_repository.py:70–91`; `backend/app/repositories/sqlalchemy/user_repository.py:36–46,55–65`.

**Problem/new executed evidence:** The helper counts a complete subquery before fetching the page; empty total=0 fails the `total_pages > 0` short-circuit and still executes the data query. The memory double executed two calls for an empty first page. For page=50,000/page_size=20/total=1M, it executed two calls and compiled OFFSET 999980. PostgreSQL must produce/discard the preceding offset rows rather than seek directly to page membership, though the actual plan/read volume is unknown. Student/mentor search applies three case-insensitive `%term%` predicates; ordinary email B-tree uniqueness does not make a leading wildcard selective. Each search pays count plus page predicate evaluation, and deep pages add discard work. This is new control-flow/SQL evidence, beyond prior DATA-14's ordering correctness finding.

**Defendable growth:** Exact count typically considers the full matching relation; page work grows with offset K plus returned cap P. At the demonstrated request K=999980 and P=20. The double does not estimate query time or prove one million physical reads. For sparse searches the cost depends on total candidate users, not only response size.

**Corrected-code proposal:** Return immediately for total=0; use stable keyset pagination and optional counts for large interactive lists. If substring search is required and measured expensive, evaluate trigram/full-text rather than adding another plain B-tree; retain the existing role/permission filter.

```python
if total == 0:
    return {"items": [], "total": 0, "page": page,
            "page_size": page_size, "total_pages": 0}
query = query.where(User.id > after_id).order_by(User.id).limit(page_size + 1)
```

The cursor example is an alternative repository/API contract, not a drop-in replacement for page numbers. If the UI requires exact page totals, preserve them through a measured alternative instead of silently changing behavior. Proposed measurement: count DB statements and p50/p95 at 10k/100k/1M users with empty, common and rare search terms; first/last/deep pages under equal cache conditions. Record EXPLAIN buffers, actual rows and index write/storage cost. Verify role isolation, stable ordering, wildcard semantics and pagination without duplicates/skips.

title: Refresh rotation continuously enlarges an authentication table without cleanup
block:
### PERF-DATA-05 — Refresh rotation continuously enlarges an authentication table without cleanup

**Impact:** Medium, long-term growth hypothesis. **Category:** database. **Review disposition:** Required (no prefix). **Location:** `backend/app/models/refresh_token.py:11–20`; `backend/app/repositories/sqlalchemy/refresh_token_repository.py:15–36`; migration `backend/alembic/versions/c592774b16d3_initial_migration.py:100–112`.

**Problem/new evidence:** Each login/rotation inserts a new RefreshToken. Revocation only updates revoked_at and valid lookup tests expires_at; no scheduled expired/revoked-row purge or expires_at cleanup index exists in the owned chain. Read-only auth context confirms insertion on each rotation. User deactivation retains rows; only physical deletion cascades. The token_hash index avoids a blanket full-table-scan claim for ordinary refresh lookup, but expired rows continue consuming heap/index/vacuum/backup storage, while per-user revoke_all must identify a user's active tokens without a user-leading index.

**Defendable growth:** At R persisted login/rotations per day, after D days without purge the table receives approximately R×D rows. An illustrative workload of 1,000 active sessions rotating hourly yields 24,000 rows/day and 8.76M/year; that is a workload model, not observed production traffic. Unknown actual session behavior determines urgency. Prior BUS-01/DATA-04 identity/replay defects remain separate correctness context: pruning does not fix them.

**Corrected-code proposal:** Define a short revoked-token replay-detection retention window and expiry retention, delete eligible rows in bounded batches, and evaluate an expiry index plus user-active lookup index using actual plans. Keep tokens needed for family replay detection until its security window ends; clean them only after implementing correct identity/rotation policy.

```sql
WITH doomed AS (
  SELECT id FROM refresh_tokens
  WHERE expires_at < :retention_cutoff
  ORDER BY expires_at, id LIMIT :batch_size
)
DELETE FROM refresh_tokens t USING doomed d WHERE t.id = d.id;
```

A forward migration can add (expires_at,id) when justified; rollout concurrently if the table is large. Proposed measurement: sample daily inserts, pg_total_relation_size, expired/revoked fraction, vacuum/backup time and EXPLAIN on hash lookup/revoke/purge at 100k/1M/10M rows. Measure bounded purge lock/WAL effects and verify no live session or retained replay evidence is deleted.
verification: Confirmed cited source mechanism and surrounding call path; static review, not a newly executed integration/load test.

return await user_service.get_students(

Even unchanged duplicate entries are appended individually to applied output, and changed/conflicting repeated entries produce per-item processing. from typing import Annotated

def unique_cells(items: list[JournalEntryUpdate]) -> list[JournalEntryUpdate]:

    return items

JournalBatch = Annotated[
    list[JournalEntryUpdate], Field(max_length=500), AfterValidator(unique_cells)
]
```

### SEC-BUS-01 — Cross-user refresh produces a privileged access grant: service-level confirmation of BUS-01

**Impact: Critical. Category: OWASP API2 Broken Authentication / CWE-287. Review disposition: Critical:.**
**Owned locations:** backend/app/core/security.py:60-72; backend/app/services/auth_service.py:41-51,69-101.

**New evidence and realistic exploit:** The old report tested token generation. This audit executed the original login and refresh service methods with the original generator/HMAC functions and repository doubles matching the hash-only first-valid-row lookup. A synthetic administrator login was stored first, then a student login at the same frozen second; token equality was true and the student's refresh returned an access JWT whose subject was the administrator ID. This verifies the entire service resolution path, without claiming PostgreSQL ordering is guaranteed. Production exploitability is conditional on another account's valid colliding row being chosen: unordered first-row selection permits that choice. An attacker need not know the signing secret or victim ID; synchronizing their own issuance with another user's issuance supplies the same bearer credential. Critical remains appropriate for possible administrator impersonation, rather than a universally deterministic takeover of a selected victim.

**Source:** refresh issuance contains only exp/iat; AuthService.refresh ignores decoded identity and uses db_token.user_id. No subject or random jti can distinguish colliding sessions; token_hash is not unique in the read-only model context.

**Corrected proposal:** Add subject, token purpose and unpredictable jti, verify all three, and atomically consume exactly the stored credential bound to its subject. Illustrative issuance:

```python
def create_refresh_token(user_id: int) -> str:
    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    return jwt.encode({
        "sub": str(user_id), "type": "refresh", "jti": secrets.token_urlsafe(32),
        "iat": int(now.timestamp()),
        "exp": int((now + timedelta(days=settings.REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRE_DAYS)).timestamp()),
    }, settings.JWT_REFRESH_SECRET_KEY, algorithm="HS256")
```

Change every issuance call, including password recovery. In rotation, require type=refresh, parse/validate sub and jti, and use UPDATE ... WHERE token_hash=:hash AND user_id=:subject AND revoked_at IS NULL AND expires_at>:now RETURNING user_id. A unique hash constraint plus invalidation of legacy ambiguous credentials prevents residual collisions; keep consumption/new issuance in one transaction. Freeze time for multi-user issuance, same-second rotation and logout isolation; run separate-session replay tests against disposable PostgreSQL after authorization. Only the in-memory resolution trace was executed here.

### SEC-BUS-02 — SMTP STARTTLS accepts an unauthenticated server certificate

**Impact: High. Category: CWE-295 Improper Certificate Validation / CWE-319. Review disposition: Critical:.**
**Owned location:** backend/app/services/email_service.py:24-29.

**Problem and exploit:** server.starttls() supplies no SSLContext. Installed Python 3.12 smtplib.SMTP.starttls creates ssl._create_stdlib_context() when context is absent; the inspected context had verify_mode=CERT_NONE and check_hostname=False. Encryption therefore authenticates neither the issuing CA nor SMTP hostname. An on-path attacker able to intercept outbound SMTP can advertise STARTTLS, present an arbitrary certificate, receive server.login credentials, and receive verification/password-reset codes sent afterward. Those codes are login/recovery capabilities, so the impact extends beyond mail confidentiality. This requires network interception or a compromised route/DNS; it is not claimed remotely exploitable through arbitrary HTTP input.

**Exact source evidence:** `server.starttls()` immediately precedes `server.login(settings.SMTP_USER, settings.SMTP_PASSWORD)` and `server.send_message(message)`. AuthService supplies actual verification/reset codes in message bodies.

**Corrected code:**

```python
with smtplib.SMTP(settings.SMTP_HOST, settings.SMTP_PORT, timeout=10) as server:
    server.ehlo()
    server.starttls(context=ssl.create_default_context())
    server.ehlo()
    server.login(settings.SMTP_USER, settings.SMTP_PASSWORD)
    server.send_message(message)
```

Import ssl. Use a deliberately configured CA bundle if the organization requires a private CA; never turn verification off to make delivery pass. Proposed verification: controlled local SMTP fixtures with an untrusted certificate and trusted-but-wrong hostname must fail before AUTH or message transmission; trusted correct-host delivery must succeed. No SMTP connections were made in this audit.

### SEC-BUS-03 — Password recovery leaves previously stolen access tokens usable

**Impact: High. Category: CWE-613 Insufficient Session Expiration / OWASP API2. Review disposition: Required (no prefix).**
**Owned locations:** backend/app/services/auth_service.py:194-198,302-305; backend/app/core/security.py:47-54.

**Problem and exploit:** Setting/resetting the password changes password_hash and revokes refresh rows only. Access JWTs contain no session/password epoch. Read-only dependency context (core/deps.py:33-52) verifies signature/expiry and loads the current nondeleted user, with no credential-version check. An attacker holding an access credential from before the victim's successful recovery can continue acting as that account until its expiry, including privileged operations for a stolen staff credential. The default access lifetime is 30 minutes; this is a bounded continued-compromise window, not an indefinite session or a claim that logout must always revoke stateless JWTs. Unlike old BUS-05's reset-grant replay, this path needs no reset grant at all after recovery.

**Corrected proposal:** Increment a persisted auth_version on every password change/recovery, atomically with the password write and refresh revocation. Include that version in all access tokens and compare it with the already-loaded user in authentication:

```python
user.password_hash = await asyncio.to_thread(hash_password, new_password)
user.auth_version += 1
await self.revoke_all_user_tokens(user.id)
access_token = create_access_token(user.id, user.role, auth_version=user.auth_version)
```

Extend generator/DTO/model/migration deliberately; reject missing/old versions after rollout rather than silently accepting legacy credentials. The dependency should validate `payload["auth_version"] == user.auth_version`. Concurrent recovery should serialize/version the user update so older grants cannot win afterward. Proposed validation: issue access+refresh, perform successful recovery, assert both old credentials fail and the new pair succeeds, for student and privileged users. Source trace establishes the omission; no live recovery request was performed.
verification: Confirmed no credential epoch in access JWT or current-user check; continued validity bounded by expiry.

### SEC-BUS-04 — Financial posting can cross accounting-period closure without rechecking the policy

**Impact: Medium. Category: CWE-367 TOCTOU / OWASP API5 Broken Function Level Authorization. Review disposition: Required (no prefix).**
**Owned locations:** backend/app/services/finance_service.py:83-99,503-526,1597-1627.

**New path relative to BUS-02:** The previous concurrency finding concerned credit/refund totals. Here an accountant's payment reads an open (or absent) AccountingPeriod, an administrator closes that month and commits, then the already-authorized posting inserts/commits its payment dated into that now-closed month. No shared lock protects the check and closure; the close updates a different table than the ledger INSERT. The advertised rule rejects writes dated into a closed period, and sequential test_period_close_enforcement verifies that rule but cannot exercise this interleaving. This is a static reachable two-session trace, not an executed database race. It does not classify legitimate late payment settlement of an old obligation as forbidden.

**Corrected proposal:** Every posting takes a transaction-scoped shared advisory lock for its affected accounting month before checking status; close/reopen take the exclusive counterpart before looking up/creating/updating that month. This also covers absent period rows, where SELECT FOR UPDATE alone cannot lock a nonexistent row:

```python
period_key = year * 12 + month - 1
await db.execute(select(func.pg_advisory_xact_lock_shared(1701, period_key)))
await self._check_period_open(occurred_at)
```

For close/reopen use pg_advisory_xact_lock(1701, period_key), then read/change state. For void/refund lock both original/current month keys in deterministic sorted order. Retain all locks through commit, and apply the distinct BUS-02 student/account serialization to aggregate money mutations. This permits concurrent writers within an open month while closure waits for authorized in-flight work. Proposed separate-session test pauses posting after its initial check, closes concurrently, and verifies one serial order: posting completes before closure or observes closed and rejects; it must never commit as a post-close unchecked write.

### SEC-DATA-01 — VM Redis publication allows authentication-state tampering and worker payload injection

**Impact:** High. **Category:** OWASP API8:2023 Security Misconfiguration; CWE-306, CWE-502. **Review disposition:** Critical:. **Location:** `backend/scripts/setup_free_tier_vm.sh:44–53,69`; owned connection context `backend/app/core/redis.py:17–26`.

**Problem/exploit:** The script publishes Redis with `-p "${REDIS_PORT}:6379"` on every interface, supplies neither ACL credentials nor TLS, and advertises a public-IP Redis URL. A client that can reach that port can read or replace verification/reset records, remove rate-limit state and manipulate job keys without CRM authentication. If an ARQ worker uses this Redis, a Redis writer can insert a serialized queued payload: installed ARQ's `deserialize_job_raw` defaults to `pickle.loads` before checking its job fields, so payload deserialization can execute code with worker credentials. The application's WorkerSettings has no safer serializer override. PostgreSQL is also bound to every interface, but its generated password means it is not equivalent to unauthenticated Redis.

**Evidence:** Docker Redis is run with only name/restart/port/volume/image flags. In installed ARQ, `arq/jobs.py:292–302` sets `deserializer = pickle.loads`; `arq/worker.py:519–520` calls it for the fetched job. These are observed source facts. Exploitation needs permitted network ingress, and the code-execution branch needs a connected running worker; cloud/host firewall policy was not inspected and no remote test or exploit ran. The orchestrator additionally queried the existing onboarding container from redis:7-alpine using read-only `redis-cli CONFIG GET protected-mode bind`: protected-mode was `no` and bind was `* -::*`; the image command was `["redis-server"]`. This corroborates the local image baseline accepting connections on all interfaces without protected-mode denial. Local compose still publishes only loopback. No VM/cloud firewall policy or future deployed image configuration was verified, so this observation does not prove Internet reachability.

**Corrected-code proposal:** The following shell excerpt replaces the port/image portion of the existing container command. Publish a private interface or loopback, restrict cloud/host firewall sources and introduce Redis ACL/TLS settings consistently for producer and worker. Use a data-only serializer as defense in depth, matching producer/consumer with versioned payloads; this does not authorize an untrusted Redis writer.

```bash
-p "127.0.0.1:${REDIS_PORT}:6379" \
-v /etc/imkon/redis.conf:/usr/local/etc/redis/redis.conf:ro \
redis:7-alpine redis-server /usr/local/etc/redis/redis.conf
```

```python
redis_settings = RedisSettings.from_dsn(settings.REDIS_URL)
```

For a separate Cloud Run client, bind an explicitly private VM IP, allow only its VPC sources, and use a `rediss://` ACL-backed DSN; loopback alone would break remote clients. Proposed verification: from an unauthorized network confirm connection denial; from an authorized network confirm unauthenticated command denial; test producer/worker serializer compatibility using harmless fixtures.
verification: Confirmed all-interface unauthenticated Redis launch and host/port-only ARQ config. External reachability and worker deployment remain conditional.

title: Local uploads enter container images and remote build artifacts
block:
### SEC-DATA-02 — Local uploads enter container images and remote build artifacts

**Impact:** High, conditional on operational uploads in the local build context and broader artifact access. **Category:** OWASP API8:2023; CWE-200. **Review disposition:** Critical:. **Location:** `backend/Dockerfile:29–35`; `backend/.dockerignore:1–15`; `backend/scripts/gcp_deploy.sh:39–40`.

**Problem/exploit:** `COPY --chown=appuser:appgroup storage/ ./storage/` embeds every existing upload in the runtime image. Docker ignores .gitignore exclusions; .dockerignore excludes environment files but does not exclude storage. The local deployer submits the current backend directory to Cloud Build. A registry reader, build operator or exported-cache reader can recover private student/mentor documents from layers without the application's ownership check. Deleting a live document does not remove a previously published immutable layer. This is a distinct disclosure channel from prior API-01's HTTP StaticFiles access.

**Evidence:** Explicit storage COPY and missing storage exclusion. No operational upload contents or registry permissions were inspected. A clean CI checkout normally does not contain ignored operational uploads; this finding specifically concerns local builds or upload-bearing contexts, not an assertion that CI already leaked data.

**Corrected-code proposal:** Remove the storage COPY and exclude storage from the context. Create empty runtime directories; use private persistent storage for uploaded objects. Inspect and retire affected historical images/build caches according to actual access and retention policies.

```dockerignore
storage/
scripts/.seed_cache/
```

```dockerfile
RUN mkdir -p /app/storage && chown -R appuser:appgroup /app/storage
```

Proposed verification: build with harmless sentinel uploads in a disposable context, assert the sent context and resulting image/layers contain no sentinel, and validate normal upload/download behavior with the chosen persistent backend.
verification: Confirmed storage COPY and absent Docker exclusion. Google Cloud Build upload also needs explicit .gcloudignore; Docker ignore alone is insufficient.

title: Bootstrap and administrator provisioning expose secrets to logs and process arguments
block:
### SEC-DATA-03 — Bootstrap and administrator provisioning expose secrets to logs and process arguments

**Impact:** Medium. **Category:** CWE-532, CWE-214; OWASP API8:2023. **Review disposition:** Required (no prefix). **Location:** `backend/scripts/setup_free_tier_vm.sh:34–40,65–68`; `backend/scripts/seed_admin.py:20–22,70–89`.

**Problem/exploit:** The VM script prints the generated PostgreSQL password and a full password-bearing DSN to stdout. Session recording, copied troubleshooting output or shared provisioning logs can then provide database access to someone who was meant to see only setup status. Its container launch also passes the password in argv. Noninteractive seed-admin explicitly requires `--password`, making the superadmin credential visible to process inspection permitted by the host and potentially shell history. This is separate from prior DATA-01's fixed demo password.

**Evidence:** The password echo/DSN interpolation and argparse option are explicit; no real secret values were read. Local process visibility depends on host permissions and isolation; no unauthenticated remote process reader is assumed.

**Corrected-code proposal:** Print variable names/status only. Read the admin password through a protected file descriptor/stdin; retain getpass for interactive use. Mount a restricted PostgreSQL password file through the image-supported POSTGRES_PASSWORD_FILE mechanism rather than passing its value on argv. Save credentials to the operator's secret store through its secure channel.

```python
parser.add_argument("--password-stdin", action="store_true")
password = sys.stdin.readline().rstrip("\n") if args.password_stdin else getpass("Password: ")
```

```bash
-e POSTGRES_PASSWORD_FILE=/run/secrets/postgres_password \
-v /etc/imkon/postgres_password:/run/secrets/postgres_password:ro
```

Preserve password validation and protect the input/file before provisioning. Proposed verification: a dummy credential must not occur in captured stdout, shell argv or status output.
verification: Confirmed cited source mechanism and surrounding call path; static review, not a newly executed integration/load test.

title: Deactivation preserves identifiable user and notification data indefinitely
block:
### SEC-DATA-04 — Deactivation preserves identifiable user and notification data indefinitely

**Impact:** Medium. **Category:** CWE-359; personal-data retention. **Review disposition:** Required (no prefix). **Location:** `backend/app/repositories/sqlalchemy/base_repository.py:52–61`; `backend/app/models/user.py:22–38`; `backend/app/models/notification_log.py:24–39`; `backend/app/models/document.py:15–25`.

**Problem/exploit:** soft_delete only flips is_deleted/deleted_at. Names, email, birth date, student/parent phone, chat binding and photo paths persist, while documents and notification recipient fields have independent lifetimes. Context confirms DELETE user calls soft_delete and revokes tokens without anonymizing PII or scheduling erasure. There is no owned retention/purge mechanism. An authorized operator or later storage/database compromise retains access to identities of long-deactivated users. This is a distinct retained-data exposure, not a claim that soft deletion itself violates an identified jurisdiction or that financial history should be destroyed.

**Evidence:** Only two fields change on deletion; model fields remain. Ledger foreign keys deliberately RESTRICT physical user deletion, so blindly deleting users would conflict with audit/financial preservation. The repository-wide retention/purge search found no implemented cleanup path; external operator policies/backups are unknown.

**Corrected-code proposal:** Define separate deactivation and approved erasure workflows. Keep a surrogate financial identity and lawfully required financial/audit history, anonymize unnecessary profile fields after a configured retention period, delete eligible private objects/recipient identifiers and expire backup copies under a documented policy.

```python
user.email = f"erased-{user.id}@invalid.example"
user.first_name = "Erased"
user.last_name = str(user.id)
user.phone = user.parent_phone = None
user.date_of_birth = user.parent_telegram_chat_id = None
user.password_hash = None
```

This is only the profile portion: object deletion must follow commit-safe, retryable orchestration and legal retention exceptions. Proposed verification: seed harmless PII, deactivate/erase, enumerate profile/object/notification/audit stores and assert expected retained versus removed fields.
verification: Confirmed soft delete retains PII; legal/operational retention durations unknown. Deferred pending owner policy, no claim soft deletion itself is illegal.

title: Mutable release inputs execute with build or deployment privileges
block:
### SEC-DATA-05 — Mutable release inputs execute with build or deployment privileges

**Impact:** Medium. **Category:** OWASP API10:2023 Unsafe Consumption; CWE-494/CWE-829. **Review disposition:** Required (no prefix). **Location:** `backend/requirements.txt:1–18`; `backend/Dockerfile:1–15`; `.github/workflows/deploy-backend.yml:80–108,124–131`; `.github/workflows/deploy-frontend.yml:24–35,95–102`; `backend/scripts/setup_free_tier_vm.sh:15–18`.

**Problem/exploit:** Python releases resolve open lower-bound ranges without an authoritative transitive lock/hash set. CI tests one resolution, Docker resolves another and the migration job installs a third unpinned set after Google authentication, with the production DB URL available. Actions use mutable major tags; the VM downloads and immediately executes an unversioned installer with system-service privileges. A compromised dependency/action/upstream installer can run in a credential-bearing release or root provisioning boundary. No compromise was observed, and TLS verification remains enabled; this is a supply-chain trust path, not an advisory-based runtime exploit claim. Frontend npm ci does preserve its lockfile, and same-workflow artifact download is not an independent untrusted-PR artifact path.

**Corrected-code proposal:** Produce a reviewed Python 3.12 transitive lock with hashes and use it consistently for tests/image/migrations, pin reviewed action commit SHAs and image digests, install Docker via a verified package repository, and keep build/package execution separate from the minimally privileged deploy job. Prefer scoped workload identity over a long-lived key; select one auth mechanism instead of providing both mutually exclusive auth inputs.

```dockerfile
COPY requirements.lock .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir --require-hashes --prefix=/install -r requirements.lock
```

```yaml
permissions:
  contents: read
```

Grant id-token write only in the isolated deploy job that needs WIF; cloud IAM must separately restrict deploy/migration identities. SHA/digest values must come from verified releases, not invented placeholders. Proposed verification: frozen install fails on altered artifacts, identical wheel graph ships/tests, and a build job has no production credentials.

**Dependency triage — FYI (not additional vulnerability IDs):** Snapshot python-jose 3.5.0 GHSA-3qf3-8w2g-rqmx needs asymmetric-key/HMAC confusion prerequisites; the traced application uses HS256 shared secrets and no asymmetric verification keys. ecdsa 0.19.2 signing-timing advisories lack a traced signing path under HS256. PyJWT advisories concern a different installed JWT implementation than the app's jose. AnyIO process-pool advisories lack a process-pool path. urllib3 2.7.0 advisories require specific proxy or streamed untrusted compressed/chunked response behavior; owned demo downloads use urllib.request, and GCS calls use a configured trusted storage service. No demonstrated exploitable application path for these snapshot flags was established. Recheck before the next release and by 2026-10-21; update affected packages when the resolved shipping graph/configuration establishes reachability. No clean-bill-of-health claim follows from this partial snapshot.
verification: Confirmed mutable dependency/action/image/installer inputs; installed advisory flags are FYI, not separately proven exploits.
